sections.h2: Where is Springdale, Arkansas, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Springdale is a city in Northwest Arkansas that sits in two counties, Washington and Benton. It covers about 49.7 square miles on the Springfield Plateau in the Ozarks, at an elevation of 1,335 feet.

Neighbors include Cave Springs and Lowell to the north, Elm Springs and Tontitown to the west, and Johnson and Fayetteville to the south, with Rogers and Bentonville close by. The Census Bureau counted 84,161 people in 2020, which made Springdale the fourth most populous city in Arkansas, and estimates 90,685 for July 1, 2025. The city grew 133 percent between the 1990 and 2010 censuses.

The two-county location is the first thing a seller should check. Your parcel belongs to either the Washington County or the Benton County tax system, and the assessor, collector and recorder you deal with depend on which side of the line the lot falls.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Springdale homes and households?
sections.html:
Springdale has 2.94 people per household and a high share of renters. The figures below are Census Bureau QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024.

MeasureSpringdale
Owner-occupied housing rate53.4%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$261,800
Median gross rent$1,071
Households29,624
Persons per household2.94
Median household income$69,787
Persons in poverty13.4%
Mean travel time to work19.3 minutes
Foreign-born persons26.6%
Language other than English at home (age 5+)40.3%

With 53.4 percent of homes owner-occupied, nearly half of occupied units are rented. Landlords who own a rental house here, and heirs who inherit one with a tenant inside, make up a real share of local sellers.

The language figure matters in a practical way. Springdale is described as home to the largest Marshallese community in the United States, and the Marshall Islands opened a consulate in the city in 2008. If a seller or family member is more comfortable in another language, a good buyer or title company should offer plain-language documents and, where needed, an interpreter.

sections.h2: What is the economy behind Springdale housing?
sections.html:
Springdale's economy is anchored by poultry and food processing, and Tyson Foods has its world headquarters in the city. The Springdale Chamber of Commerce list of top employers, as reproduced on Wikipedia, names these:

  • Tyson Foods, 4,300 employees
  • George's, 2,500
  • Springdale Public Schools, 2,235
  • Cargill Meat Solutions, 1,200
  • Northwest Medical Center-Springdale, 900

Arkansas law named Springdale the Poultry Capital of the World in 2013. Other manufacturers listed in the area include Apex Tool Group, Ball Corporation, Dayco Products and Pratt and Whitney. The census figure for average travel time to work is 19.3 minutes.

Employer headcounts shift from year to year, so treat the numbers above as a snapshot and check with the chamber for current figures.

Springdale Public Schools is the district for nearly all of the city, and it is described as the largest district in Arkansas, with roughly 23,000 students. It began on January 7, 1884 as Springdale School District No. 50 and now spans Springdale, Elm Springs, Tontitown and parts of Fayetteville, Goshen and Johnson in Washington County, plus most of Springdale's Benton County portion including the former town of Bethel Heights.

Springdale High School and Har-Ber High School serve grades 10 through 12, and the Don Tyson School of Innovation serves grades 6 through 12. Har-Ber and Hellstern Middle School opened in 2005 on land bought in 2002. Private options include Shiloh Christian School.

Bethel Heights merged into Springdale when it was annexed on August 21, 2020. Owners of houses there should check that their records reflect the city and district boundaries.

sections.h2: What weather and ground conditions should Springdale sellers expect?
sections.html:
Springdale has a humid subtropical climate with cold snaps and hot stretches. The July average high is 89 degrees, the January average low is 29 degrees, and the city sees about 57 days a year above 90 degrees. The record high is 111 degrees from 1954, and the record low is minus 24 degrees from 1899.

An EF3 tornado struck Springdale on March 30, 2022 and injured seven people. Roof and siding claims are a common history item for houses in the area, so keep any insurance paperwork and repair invoices together.

The ground matters too. Springdale sits on exposed Mississippian limestone, and Washington County is known for karst features such as springs, sinkholes and caves. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says solution and collapse sinkholes are abundant in the Boone Formation, the limestone beneath the Springfield Plateau. A sinkhole or foundation settling is a condition a buyer's inspector will want explained, and it is one reason some owners prefer an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What roads, transit and airports serve Springdale?
sections.html:
Springdale is reached by Interstate 49, which runs along US 62 and US 71 and is the only fully controlled-access route through the area. Former US 71 is now US 71B, Highway 412 runs east toward Beaver Lake, and the Bella Vista Bypass opened in October 2021. Ozark Regional Transit provides public transit.

Springdale Municipal Airport handles general aviation, while commercial flights use Northwest Arkansas National Airport in Highfill.

sections.h2: How do city permits and offices work when selling in Springdale?
sections.html:
The Building Department lists City Hall at 201 Spring Street as its address, and the number is 479-750-8114. The city website lists building, planning, engineering and code enforcement pages, but the pages we opened only gave contact details, so ask staff directly what applies to your property.

The city runs on a mayor-council system. Eight council members are elected, two from each of four wards, and the council meets on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month.

Before listing or accepting an offer, a Springdale seller can do these things:

  • Call the Building Department about permits for any remodel, roof, deck or addition.
  • Ask Neighborhood Services whether any open complaint exists on the property.
  • Confirm the parcel's county, since this decides who collects the tax.
  • Collect the deed, any lease, and tenant contact details if the house is rented.

sections.h2: How is property tax handled for a Springdale house?
sections.html:
For parcels in Washington County, property tax is due October 15, with a 10 percent penalty on late payment and 10 percent annual interest on real estate. Tax statements are mailed each year, and the collector's office says to call 479-444-1526 if yours has not arrived by April 15. The Washington County Assessor says the county's four-year reappraisal cycle started in 2023, and Washington County homeowners have a homestead credit of up to $600 on a primary residence. Taxable value increases from reappraisal are capped at 5 percent a year on a homestead. Seniors and disabled owners can claim a freeze.

The state transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of sale price, which is $330 on a $100,000 sale.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Springdale seller?
sections.html: A cash sale can suit landlords with tenants in place, heirs who live out of state, and owners with deferred repairs. A listing may bring a higher price on a house that is in good shape, so get an agent's opinion too. Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on houses as-is, and we do not quote a figure until we know the property.

faqs.q: Is Springdale in Washington County or Benton County?
faqs.a: Both. Springdale is split between the two counties. Look up your parcel to see which county assesses and bills it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Springdale, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 90,685 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 84,161, making it the fourth most populous city in Arkansas.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Springdale?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a median value of $261,800 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, not an appraisal of any single house.

faqs.q: When is Washington County property tax due?
faqs.a: October 15. Payments after that date carry a 10 percent penalty, and real estate also accrues 10 percent annual interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Springdale rental with a tenant living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers who pay cash accept a tenant in place, but read the lease and talk to the buyer about timing before you sign.

faqs.q: Does a sinkhole or foundation problem stop a sale?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A buyer will want an inspection and may lower the price, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is without repairs.
